figures.alt: Matte-black exterior deadbolt, latch bolt, and aligned strike plate on a white door
figures.caption: Check the door slab, jamb, strike, and existing bore before ordering a deadbolt. A shifted frame or soft material can mimic a lock problem even when the cylinder itself still turns.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Aligned black door hinges and even meeting-edge spacing on white exterior doors
figures.caption: Measure the backset and bore, then make sure the door closes squarely before forcing a new bolt into the strike. Lock hardware works best when the opening is already aligned and supported.

figures.alt: Localized moisture-softened wood at the lower corner of an exterior door jamb
figures.caption: Use corrosion-resistant exterior hardware and test the lock from both sides with the door fully closed. If the jamb is wet, soft, or moving, repair that condition before treating a new deadbolt as the whole solution.
